source_title: Bethesda Previews Two Big Fallout 76 Updates
source_excerpt:
Bethesda has launched a new Fallout 76 Public Test Server build previewing content planned for the game's next two major update windows. Some of the features included in the latest PTS release are planned to join Fallout 76 as early as December 2026, with the rest expected to materialize in 2027.
Bethesda first outlined both additions in September, while outlining its Fallout 76 content roadmap for the rest of 2026 and 2027 . As usual, the upcoming features first arrived on the game's experimental PTS channel, with testing for them now officially expanding beyond PC to include the Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5.
Fallout 76's December 2026 Update Is Headlined by World Pets
Dominik Bošnjak / GameRant | Source image: Bethesda Game Studios
An edited Fallout 76 screenshot depicting a crouching character holding a scoped lever-action rifle (adorned with an olive green vinyl/skin featuring a bunch of yellow eyes and wearing a robot headgear mask obtained from Fasnacht. Dominik Bošnjak / GameRant | Source image: Bethesda
The first of the two additions is Fallout 76 's much-anticipated World Pets update , which Bethesda plans to release on December 1. The feature will allow existing C.A.M.P. pets to accompany players while exploring Appalachia, introducing commands to make them stay put, remain neutral, attack enemies, or focus on protecting their owner. Since pets will be able to participate in combat, they will also be revivable with Stimpaks when downed. The system will come with some restrictions, like not allowing pets in Raids or Shelters.
World Pets will also introduce a sizable progression system, with companions able to reach level 200. Progress is tracked by species rather than by individual creature, which should streamline gameplay and result in a more accessible leveling loop. The progression grind can improve pet health and damage while also unlocking player bonuses and cosmetic rewards such as Fallout 76 outfits , backpacks, and Player Titles. Pets can also learn passive abilities, with up to two active at once. Bethesda recently expanded the system so that abilities learned by one species can be used with another.
Two iconic game characters. One impossible mashup. Can you name them both?
Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!
The December 2026 update will extend beyond companions with a broader rework of Fallout 76 's Skyline Valley region . Bethesda has refined parts of the map's mountains and hillsides, added new pathways and vegetation, and improved its lighting and weather. Skyline Valley will also gain Bounty Hunting, with the Trading Post serving as a hub where players can obtain targets from a reprogrammed Robobrain named Marshal Canton. Another new questline arriving in December will revolve around collectible glass canisters that appear to contain living brain specimens, with finding the first one setting players on the trail of the rest.
Hideouts Are Coming to Fallout 76 in Spring 2027
The second major feature currently being tested on the PTS is Hideouts, which Bethesda plans to release in spring 2027. These new bounty encounters are intended to bridge the gap between earlier endgame content and Raids, with access revolving around "Leads" that also determine difficulty. Four tiers are currently planned: Basic, Challenging, Lethal, and Marked. The lower difficulties target less experienced characters, while the upper tiers are designed around powerful late-game builds and coordinated teams. Higher-level Leads can be crafted from lower-tier ones and other resources, while accessing Marked difficulty also requires a resource called Drifter Intel. Console players wanting to participate in the Fallout 76 Public Test Server can get started by joining Bethesda's official Discord server . Their PC peers can do the same by simply downloading the PTS client via Steam.
Fallout 76 World Pets Console PTS Update Patch Notes
Every C.A.M.P. Pet you currently own can be brought out into the world as a travel partner. In your Pip-Boy, you’ll find a new tab under the “Stats” menu that shows your entire catalogue of Pets. Selecting one of the pets in that menu will summon them beside you. Ready for the many adventures that await you! Once this update releases, all pets will be able to be used in your C.A.M.P. or out in the Wasteland.
Important Note: All accounts have been given access to 1 pet of each species to assist in your testing purposes. When World Pets releases, you will only have the pets you have previously obtained.
With your faithful companion beside you, you’re ready to take on the wasteland. When looking at your pet, an interact button will appear that allows you to issue one of the commands below. The emote wheel has been updated to provide a way to quickly access these commands as well.
Stay – The pet will remain at its current location until you give the follow command, or you move too far away.
Attack – Send your pet to attack your target! Pinging a target while your Pet is active will also send them charging towards your target.
Protect – Your pet will follow you and only attack if you take damage. When it comes to having your pet follow you around, the only places you won’t be able to take your furry friend is into a Raid or a Shelter. Pets will also not be able to swim underwater.
All pets have the same amount of HP regardless of their species. You can increase pet HP by leveling up and unlocking Pet Prowess combat upgrades.
Allowing your pet to take too much damage will put them into a downed state. Requiring you to rush to their side and deliver a Stimpak to get them back up. Clearing out all nearby enemies will also pick your pet up, but they’ll still require a Stimpak to get them back to full health.
Pets will not be affected by Radiation or Diseases, and they cannot be hurt by other players. Other players can give your pet a Stimpak though. So, if see someone’s Glowing Radhog is down in the dumps, be a good Samaritan and give it a quick pick-me-up.
All pets can attack enemies through a series of melee attacks. Dogs will bite and Deathclaws (and cats) will scratch. Radhogs, well Radhogs RAM!
Pets will never attack other players or other player’s pets even if they are hostile to you. They will only attack enemy NPCs.
You can track your Pet’s leveling progress by navigating to the Pets tab in your Pip-Boy and pressing the “Right Stick” on your controller to open the Pet Progression Menu.
Anytime that you earn XP with your World Pet active allows them to gain XP as well. They can reach a max level of 200, unlocking HP/DMG increases, increased player carry capacity, Pet Passive improvements (more on that below) as well as rewards such as outfits, backpacks, Player Titles, and more.
Don’t worry about having to level up each individual type of Dog you have though. Pets are leveled on a per species basis. Meaning that leveling your German Shepherd will bring all your dogs up to the same level. So, feel free to swap that German Shepherd out for the RoboPaw Steel Dog whenever the mood strikes.
Each pet has two passive buffs: one that grants you a useful item, and one that improves rewards in a specific type of activity/event.
These passive buffs can be applied to any pet species after they have been learned. This means that if you level up your pet Deathclaw enough to unlock the Fun-Festation 1 passive, you can have that buff be active while your Cat, Dog, or Radhog are traveling with you.
All you need to do after unlocking a passive is select the buff you want from your Pip-Boy. You can do this by navigating to the Pets page in your Pip-Boy and then press the button that appears on the bottom of your screen for “Pet Buffs”. This will take you to a list of unlocked Pet Buffs where you can choose which two buffs you would like to have activated. These can be changed at any time!
After being activated, Passive Buffs are displayed in your Pip-Boy under the Effects tab.

The Skyline Valley environment has received some love with the team doing some landscaping work to improve how it feels to travel around the region. In some cases, entire mountains and hillsides have been reworked, in others new pathways have been laid with extra trees and vegetation to give the region the extra environmental love it deserves. All this combined with the lighting and the weather improvements for the region really set the mood.
Local tour guides recommend the following locations:
Head on over to “The Trading Post” which now acts as the hub for Bounty Hunting in Skyline Valley.
There you will find Marshal Canton, a reprogrammed Robo-Brain who was probably left out in the storm for too long. Marshal Canton has been tracking a number of dangerous visitors who have arrived in the valley and is ready to reward you for taking them down.
Bounty Hunting in Skyline Valley introduces new factions to the experience. Prepare to fight Super Mutants, Mothman Cultists, The Lost, and more.
Skyline Valley – New Collectible Questline
While you’re taking in the sights of the renovated Skyline Valley, you’ll likely stumble across mysterious glass cannisters. These canisters look like they’re filled with a live brain specimen, but surely that can’t be the case. Someone must know what they’re being used for.
After collecting your first glass jar, you Pip-Boy will update with a location for you to take it to and there your adventure will begin.
This is a call to the bravest Bounty Hunters in Appalachia. Thanks to your dutiful work clearing out those villainous rapscallions, we’re starting to get a picture of where they’re all coming from.
These encampments can be found around Appalachia, and those that have made it out say they are filled with some of the biggest and baddest from the various factions around the region. It will be up to you to find leads that will direct you to where these Hideouts are and give you access you need to enter.
Arriving with four different difficulties (Basic, Challenging, Lethal, and Marked), Hideouts serve as a dynamic new challenge where you get to control the difficulty through the type of lead you craft. And of course, if you want the highest chance of getting some of the best rewards, you’ll want to clear these out on higher difficulties.
Round up your posse, bring your favorite pet, and head over to Marshall Canton at the Trading Post in Skyline Valley. There are Hideouts that need to be cleaned out.
Please Note: For the purposes of this testing period, The Drifter will not appear in Hideouts. Also, all rewards you obtain from completing Hideouts are TEMPORARY and don’t include any of the unique rewards we have planned for this content. The focus of this testing period is Hideout difficulty.
Finding and crafting leads on the various Hideout locations is how you’ll be able to craft your entrance key to their encampment. It will also be how you control the level of challenge too.
Basic Leads can be obtained through Daily Quests, Activities, Grunt Hunts, and from various cabinets and safes in the world. Targeted for a team of Level 20 characters.
Challenging Leads can be crafted by exchanging 3 Basic Leads and some Caps at your Tinker’s Workbench. Or by participating and completing in Head Hunts, Seasonal Public Events, Infestations, and Public Events. Targeted for a team of Level 75-100 characters.
Like Challenging Leads, Lethal Leads can be crafted by exchanging 3 Challenging Leads and some Caps. This will be your primary way of accessing this harder difficulty. They can also be found on the final season repeatable page. Targeted for a team ready to face enemies that are Level 175+.
Marked Leads are the highest challenge and can only be obtained through crafting. Costing a mixture of Lethal Leads, Caps, and Drifter Intel. Once this update is released, these leads will guarantee The Drifter’s appearance but are also significantly more challenging to complete. Targeted for late game players with strong builds and coordination.
During this PTS, Drifter Intel is only obtainable as a rare crafting outcome when Lethal Leads are crafted from Challenging ones.
The two Hideout locations for this update will be The Forever Farm in Burning Springs and Vault 63’s Immortality Sector in Skyline Valley. Designed as non-linear spaces, you will have to determine which approach is the best to tackle the challenges in front of you.
Various environmental and enemy mutations ensure that no two Hideouts runs are the same. One time you could be facing The Lost and the next a Mutated Super Mutant gang. Maybe parts of the Hideout are bathed in irradiation? You won’t know until you get in there. There are things to discover in every run.
Other potential Hideout inhabitants include Robots, Rust Raiders, and Mothman Cultists. Rust Raiders and The Lost will appear only in Hideouts within their respective regions.
These locations are not locked away from you outside of attempting them as Hideouts either. Feel free to enter either location to experience it as you would any other space. Get a feel for the layout or just run in there to defeat and loot anything foolish enough to be hanging around.
Once you start a Hideout, you will have bonus objectives to complete. Each objective will award the team with a Fallen Deputy’s Pack which contains bonus loot (reminder, loot you obtain through this pack is placeholder for this PTS). The bonus objectives will be:
Find a Fallen Deputy’s Badge inside one of the 4 hidden containers in the Hideout.
The reward for finding one of the 4 hidden containers will only be obtained if found before clearing out the Hideout gang leader.
Defeating the Hideout gang leader within a time limit.
The time limit begins once you move past the prep area of the Hideout.
Currently, the Rust Raiders will appear in the Immortality Sector and The Lost will appear in the Forever Farm. These factions are intended to exclusively appear in the Hideout that exists in their respective region.
There are occasions where only the party leader will obtain the Fallen Deputy’s Badge.
During the PTS, you will not be able to continue a Hideout after logging out or disconnection. This will not be the case upon release.
Hideouts may take a little while to spawn enemies once they are started.
While exploring a Hideout outside of the Quest, some enemies in the location may attack each other when they shouldn’t.
If you leave a Hideout while the quest is active, you will be removed form the quest and unable to rejoin. The intended flow is that players will be able to be re-added to the quest if they return.
Currently, death in a Hideout drops your loot like death in the open world. This is not intended.
The Tesla trap in the Immortality Sector is not functioning as expected.
Because we’re testing this feature in an earlier than normal state, there are a few things we want to make sure you’re aware of.
Rewards will be obtained once the quest is completed.
Consuming a new Hideout Lead will abandon any current Hideout quest currently have active.
A new Hideout quest cannot be started while you are inside of a Hideout location (Forever Farm or Immortality Sector). Please leave the Hideout before attempting to activate a new lead.
You can only join your team leader’s Hideout. Any Hideout quests started while you’re in a team, but NOT the team leader can only be completed solo.
The PTS locker (the locker outside Vault 76) has Hideout Leads to assist with your testing needs.
